flawed_step: Line 0006 incorrectly claims that every component of G=(V,M∪M') is an isolated vertex or a cycle.
counterexample: Let T have vertices {1,2} and the single edge {1,2}. Take M=M'={{1,2}}, a perfect matching. Then G has one component consisting of the edge {1,2}; it is neither an isolated vertex nor a cycle.
assessment_summary: The component classification used in the proof is false because edges common to M and M' form two-vertex, one-edge components. Thus the proof is invalid as written, although the theorem itself is true.
